title: grep & curl (and how AI uses them)

lessons.title: grep - find lines that match
lessons.body:
grep searches text for a pattern and prints the matching lines. That's it.
  grep error app.log            lines containing 'error'
  grep -i error app.log         -i = ignore case (Error, ERROR too)
  grep -r TODO .                -r = search every file under here
  grep -n error app.log         -n = show line numbers
  grep -v error app.log         -v = INVERT: lines WITHOUT 'error'
  grep -c error app.log         -c = just count the matches
  grep -E 'cat|dog' file        -E = regex (here, cat OR dog)
The magic is piping: feed another command's output into grep with |:
  ps aux | grep ssh             running processes, filtered to ssh
In security this is 80% of log analysis - that's exactly what wire-01 is.

lessons.title: curl - talk to a URL from the terminal
lessons.body:
curl makes web requests and prints what comes back. It's your browser without the window.
  curl http://site/page         fetch the page body
  curl -I http://site           -I = headers only (HEAD request)
  curl -v http://site           -v = verbose: see the whole request/response + TLS
  curl -L http://site           -L = follow redirects (3xx)
  curl -o out.html http://site  -o = save to a file
  curl -d 'user=a&pw=b' http://site/login   -d = POST this form data
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer X' http://api   -H = add a header
curl is how you inspect what a server really sends, test an API, or check an endpoint - the first tool you reach for on the App layer.

lessons.title: Piping them together
lessons.body:
The Unix idea: small tools, chained with |, each doing one thing. Examples:
  curl -s http://site | grep -i 'password'     fetch a page, show lines mentioning password
  curl -sI http://site | grep -i server         just the Server: header
  grep -rn 'api_key' .                          hunt hardcoded secrets in a codebase
-s makes curl silent (no progress bar) so the pipe is clean. Learning to chain curl + grep + sort + uniq is the difference between staring at data and answering a question with it.

lessons.title: How AI coding tools use grep & curl
lessons.body:
When an AI coding assistant (like the one that built this repo) works in a codebase, it mostly uses the SAME tools you just learned:
  - grep / ripgrep (rg): before changing code, it searches the repo for where a function, variable, or string is defined and used - so it edits the right place and doesn't miss callers. 'Find every use of parse_packet' is just grep.
  - curl / HTTP fetch: to read documentation, test an API endpoint, or check that a local server responds, it makes the same requests curl does.
The AI isn't doing anything mystical - it reads with grep, fetches with curl, runs code, reads the output, and decides the next step. Watching how it chains these is a great way to learn the workflow yourself: the tools are the same, the loop is the same.

quiz.q: Which grep flag searches all files in a directory tree?
How do you fetch ONLY the response headers with curl?
quiz.why: -I sends a HEAD request: headers only.

quiz.q: What does `ps aux | grep ssh` do?
options: lists processes, showing only lines mentioning ssh
quiz.why: ps lists processes; grep filters that output to ssh lines.

quiz.q: When an AI coding tool needs to find where a function is used, it most likely...
options: greps the codebase for the name
quiz.why: It searches (grep/ripgrep) for the symbol - same tool you just learned.
